title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for "Mind" Exploration of Large Language Model Society
layout_note: Two large side-by-side panels: a narrow left panel for the human side (an idea note, a person icon, a role-assignment card) and a wide right panel for the automated session, which flows from a task-specifier icon down into a specified-task card, then branches with curved arrows to two role icons (AI User above, AI Assistant below, joined by a vertical double-headed arrow), with the exchanged messages stacked as a column of alternating cards on the far right that trails off in a vertical ellipsis.
grouping: Both panels are light-grey rounded rectangles with a dark outline and a bold title (one at the top of the left panel, one at the bottom of the right). Colour is tied to role: the AI User's name, icon and instruction messages are orange; the AI Assistant's name, icon and solution messages are blue; the human idea is a green card and the specified task a pink card, each with an underlined bold label at the start of its text.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with thin coloured outlines and pastel fills; no shadows. Icons are simple line or flat glyphs: a smiling person, a robotic arm for the task specifier, two robot heads for the agents tinted in their role colour. Black curved arrows with small heads; a thick double-headed vertical arrow for the conversation between the two agents. The message column is real transcript text in small sans-serif, instruction cards short and orange, solution cards tall and blue.
proposed_highlight: The automated part is the larger right panel; the two agent roles are the only coloured icons, and their colours carry through to every message they send, so the transcript column reads as an alternating dialogue without speaker labels on each card.
lesson: Give each role-playing agent a signature colour on its icon and name, then stack the dialogue as alternating message cards filled in the speaker's colour so turn-taking is visible at a glance.
notes: elements 'other' = the alternating message-card transcript column and the vertical ellipsis that marks it continues. Venue and year from the PDF first page footer (NeurIPS 2023).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: role-playing framework for autonomous cooperation between LLM agents

core.what: a left-to-right hand-off from a narrow 'Human Input' panel (idea card, role assignment) into a wide 'Role Playing Session' panel where a Task Specifier turns the idea into a specified-task card that two agents then discuss in a column of alternating chat messages

relations.form: curved arrow from the green idea card to the robot-arm Task Specifier, a short down arrow to the pink Specified Task card, then a forked arrow to the two agent icons
the AI User (orange robot) and AI Assistant (blue robot) are stacked with a double-headed vertical arrow between them
the dialogue is a right-hand column of alternating orange Instruction and blue Solution message cards, ending in a vertical ellipsis

channels.colour: role colour: orange = AI User (name, icon, instruction messages), blue = AI Assistant (name, icon, solution messages), green = human idea, pink = specified task, beige = role assignment
channels.shape: icons for actors (person, robot arm, two robots), rounded text cards for content
channels.frame: two grey rounded panels = the human side and the agent session

quality.strengths: Colour carries one meaning, the role, from the role-assignment card through the agent icons to every chat message, so the column of messages can be read as a turn-taking dialogue without labels; all content is real quoted text (idea, task, pip commands).
quality.weaknesses: The chat column takes a third of the width with small dense text that the reader need not read, while the two agents sit as small icons; the link from agents to messages is implied by colour only, with no arrow from either icon to the column; the human-input panel spends half its height on a person icon.

insights.structure: Two light-grey rounded panels side by side: a narrow 'Human Input' panel at left (idea card, human icon, role-assignment card) and a wide 'Role Playing Session' panel at right (robot-arm Task Specifier, pink specified-task card, two agent icons, and a column of chat messages).
insights.data: Everything is real example content: the human idea and specified task are quoted sentences in cards, roles are written out (Python Programmer, Stock Trader), and the dialogue column shows actual instruction and solution messages including pip commands and import lines.
insights.emphasis: Colour is tied to role throughout: orange for the AI User's name, icon and instruction messages, blue for the AI Assistant's name, icon and solution messages, green for the human idea, pink for the specified task.
insights.flow: Left to right: a curved arrow from the idea card to the Task Specifier, down to the specified task, then a branching curve to both agents, who exchange via a vertical double arrow; the transcript reads top-to-bottom alternating orange/blue, ending in a vertical ellipsis.
insights.avoid: The transcript column is set in very small text that is unreadable at print size, and the two panel titles sit at different places (top of the left panel, bottom of the right).

arrangement.units: two rounded grey panels with dark outline: 'Human Input' (left, titled top) and 'Role Playing Session' (right, titled bottom)
arrangement.inputs_as: a green card with the quoted human idea plus a beige role-assignment card
arrangement.shared: role colours (orange user, blue assistant) are shared between the role-assignment card, the agent icons and the messages
